Claim 1 is about an existing Alabama plant (2003). Claim 2 is about a new Georgia factory ("will build"). These are complementary claims describing different facilities/locations and stages (existing vs. planned). Not a conflict on scope/date.

However, the text distinguishes between "KORUS FTA" (existing) and "proposed KORUS FTA". Even if both refer to the same agreement context, one describes a rule of origin requirement, the other describes calculation options under a *proposed* version or specific section. They are not necessarily incompatible; one is a general requirement, the other is a methodological option under a proposal. However, looking closely at Claim 1 ("has") vs Claim 2 ("proposed"), they might refer to different stages of the agreement or different aspects (ROO vs RVC calculation). Given the "proposed" qualifier in Claim 2 and the definitive "has" in Claim 1, they describe different states of the agreement or different specific provisions. They are not direct contradictions on the same scope/date without more context, but Claim 2 explicitly flags "proposed".
